title.zh: 卷17 列傳第9 梁禦 若干惠 怡峯 劉亮 王德
title.en: Volume 17 Biographies 9: Liang Yu; Guo Ganhui; Yi Feng; Liu Liang; Wang De
title.raw: 卷17 列傳第9 梁禦 若干惠 怡峯 劉亮 王德 Volume 17 Biographies 9: Liang Yu; Guo Ganhui; Yi Feng; Liu Liang; Wang De

sentences.zh: 梁禦 若干惠 怡峯 劉亮 王德

translations.literal: Liang Yu; Guo Ganhui; Yi Feng; Liu Liang; Wang De
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yu — Guo Ganhui — Yi Feng — Liu Liang — Wang De

sentences.zh: 梁禦字善通，其先安定人也。

translations.literal: Liang Yu, styled Shantong, his forebears were natives of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yu, styled Shantong, came from Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 後因官北邊，遂家於武川，改姓為紇豆陵氏。

translations.literal: Later, because of official service on the northern frontier, his family settled in Wuchuan and changed surname to Hedouling.
translations.idiomatic: Later his family moved to Wuchuan on frontier duty and took the surname Hedouling.

sentences.zh: 高祖俟力提，從魏太祖征討，位至揚武將軍、定陽侯。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Siliti followed Wei's founding emperor on campaigns and reached General Who Raises Martial Might and Marquis of Dingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Siliti campaigned under Wei's founding emperor and rose to general who raises martial might and marquis of Dingyang.

sentences.zh: 禦少好學，進趨詳雅。

translations.literal: Yu from youth loved learning; in conduct he was detailed and refined.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yu loved books from boyhood and carried himself with careful grace.

sentences.zh: 及長，更好弓馬。

translations.literal: When grown, he came to love bow and horse even more.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he took even more to archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 爾朱天光西討，知禦有志略，引為左右，授宣威將軍、都將。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Tianguang campaigned west, knowing Yu had ambition and strategy, he brought him close as attendant and appointed General Who Proclaims Might and capital-guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: During Erzhu Tianguang's western campaign he saw Liang Yu's talent and kept him at his side, making him general who proclaims might and capital-guard commander.

sentences.zh: 共平關右，除鎮西將軍、東益州刺史、第一領民酋長，封白水縣伯，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Together they pacified Guan-you; he was made general who guards the west, governor of East Yizhou, first tribal chief commanding the people, enfeoffed Earl of Baishui county with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: They pacified Guan-you together; Liang Yu became general who guards the west, governor of East Yizhou, and first tribal chief commanding the people, and was enfeoffed Earl of Baishui with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 轉征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Transferred to general who campaigns west and grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general who campaigns west and grand master of splendid happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 後從賀拔岳鎮長安。

translations.literal: Later he followed Heba Yue in garrisoning Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Heba Yue in garrisoning Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 及岳被害，禦與諸將同謀翊戴太祖。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed, Yu together with the generals jointly plotted to support and install the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue was murdered, Liang Yu and the other generals plotted to raise up Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 從征侯莫陳悅，遷武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Following in the campaign against Houmochen Yue, he was transferred to martial guard general.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Houmochen Yue and was made martial guard general.

sentences.zh: 太祖既平秦隴，方欲引兵東下，雍州刺史賈顯持兩端，通使於齊神武。

translations.literal: After the Grand Progenitor had pacified Qin and Long, he was about to lead troops east; Yong Province governor Jia Xian hedged between two sides and sent envoys to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had secured Qin and Long, he prepared to march east; but Yong Province governor Jia Xian wavered and opened talks with Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 太祖微知其意，以禦為大都督、雍州刺史，領前軍先行。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor slightly knew his intent and made Yu grand commander and governor of Yong Province, leading the vanguard to go first.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai saw through the maneuver and sent Liang Yu ahead as grand commander and governor of Yong Province with the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 既與顯相見，因說顯曰：「魏室陵遲，天下鼎沸。

translations.literal: Once he met Xian, he thereupon persuaded Xian, saying: "The Wei house declines and sinks; the realm boils like a cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Jia Xian he urged him: "The Wei dynasty is failing and the empire is in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 高歡志在凶逆，梟夷非遠。

translations.literal: Gao Huan's intent is toward villainy and rebellion; execution is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan aims at treason, and his downfall cannot be far away.

sentences.zh: 宇文夏州英姿不世，算略無方，方欲扶危定傾，匡復京洛。

translations.literal: Yuwen of Xia Province has heroic bearing unmatched in his age, stratagem without measure, and is about to support the perilous and set the tipping straight and restore the capital and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai of Xia Province is a hero of his generation, unmatched in strategy, and is ready to rescue the realm and recover the capital at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 公不於此時建立功效，乃懷猶豫，恐禍不旋踵矣。

translations.literal: If you sir do not at this time establish merit and achievement but instead harbor hesitation, I fear disaster will not wait for the heel to turn."
translations.idiomatic: If you miss this chance to earn your place and keep hesitating, ruin will overtake you before you can turn around."

sentences.zh: 」顯即出迎太祖，禦遂入鎮雍州。

translations.literal: Xian thereupon went out to welcome the Grand Progenitor; Yu then entered to garrison Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xian went out at once to welcome Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, and Liang Yu took up the Yong Province garrison.

sentences.zh: 授車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry and three-division court equipage.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand general of chariots and cavalry with three-division court equipage.

sentences.zh: 子睿襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Rui inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rui inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 天和中，拜開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era he was appointed opening-office three-division court equipage.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhe era he was made opening-office three-division court equipage.

sentences.zh: 以禦佐命有功，進蔣國公。

translations.literal: Because Yu had merit in aiding the mandate, he was advanced to Duke of Jiang State.
translations.idiomatic: For Liang Yu's service in establishing the dynasty, the family was raised to Duke of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 大象末，除益州總管，加授柱國。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang he was made area commander of Yizhou with additional appointment as pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daxiang era he was made area commander of Yizhou and pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 睿將之任，而王謙舉兵，拒不受代。

translations.literal: Rui was about to take up the post when Wang Qian raised troops and refused to accept replacement.
translations.idiomatic: When Rui was on his way to take office, Wang Qian rebelled and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 仍詔睿為行軍元帥，討謙，破之。

translations.literal: Rui was still ordered campaign commander-in-chief to attack Qian and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was then ordered out as campaign commander-in-chief against Wang Qian and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 進位上柱國。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to supreme pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to supreme pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 若干惠字惠保，代郡武川人也。

translations.literal: Guo Ganhui, styled Huibao, was a native of Wuchuan in Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ganhui, styled Huibao, came from Wuchuan in Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 其先與魏氏俱起，以國為姓。

translations.literal: His forebears rose together with the Wei clan and took the state as surname.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had risen with the Wei and taken the state name as their surname.

sentences.zh: 父樹利周，從魏廣陽王深征葛榮，戰沒，贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Shulizhou followed Wei's Prince of Guangyang Shen against Ge Rong, died in battle, and was posthumously given governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shulizhou followed the Prince of Guangyang, Shen, against Ge Rong and fell in battle; the court posthumously made him governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 惠年弱冠，從爾朱榮征伐，定河北，破元顥，以功拜中堅將軍。

translations.literal: Hui at the age of weak crown followed Erzhu Rong on campaigns, stabilized Hebei, defeated Yuan Hao, and by merit was appointed general of the central guard.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty Gan Hui followed Erzhu Rong on campaign, secured Hebei, and defeated Yuan Hao; for this he was made general of the central guard.

sentences.zh: 復以別將從賀拔岳西征，解岐州圍，擒万俟醜奴，平水洛，定隴右，每力戰有功。

translations.literal: Again as separate commander he followed Heba Yue west, relieved the siege of Qi Prefecture, captured Wanqij Chounu, pacified Shuiluo, and stabilized Long-you; each time he fought hard with merit.
translations.idiomatic: As a separate commander under Heba Yue he marched west, lifted the siege of Qi, captured Wanqij Chounu, pacified Shuiluo, and secured Long-you, fighting fiercely at every step.

sentences.zh: 封北平縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed Viscount of Beiping county with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He received the viscounty of Beiping with two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 累遷鎮遠將軍、都督、直寢、征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: By successive promotion he reached general who guards the distant, area commander, direct attendants guard, general who campaigns west, and grand master of splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to general who guards the distant, area commander, direct attendants guard, general who campaigns west, and grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 及岳為侯莫陳悅所害，惠與寇洛、趙貴等同謀翊戴太祖。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed by Houmochen Yue, Hui with Kou Luo, Zhao Gui, and others jointly plotted to support and install the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue killed Heba Yue, Gan Hui joined Kou Luo, Zhao Gui, and others in raising up Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 仍從平悅，拜直閤將軍。

translations.literal: Still following in pacifying Yue, he was appointed direct-pavilion general.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign that crushed Houmochen Yue and was made direct-pavilion general.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，除右衛將軍、大都督，進爵魏昌縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, he was made right guard general and grand commander; his rank was advanced to Earl of Weichang with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Gan Hui became right guard general and grand commander and was raised to Earl of Weichang with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 出為北華州刺史，加使持節、驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of North Huazhou with additional credentials as envoy and grand general of fast cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of North Huazhou with full credentials and the rank of grand general of fast cavalry.

sentences.zh: 大統初，拜儀同三司，進爵為公，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong he was appointed three-division court equipage, advanced in rank to duke, and his fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Datong he received three-division court equipage, was raised to duke, and gained five hundred more households.

sentences.zh: 從擒竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，惠每先登陷陣。

translations.literal: Following in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and breaking Shaya, Hui each time was first to ascend and breach the formation.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaigns that took Dou Tai, recovered Hongnong, and broke Shaya, Gan Hui was always first over the ramparts and into the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 加侍中、開府，進爵長樂郡公，增邑通前二千二百戶。

translations.literal: He was added palace attendant and opening office, advanced in rank to Duke of Changle commandery, and his fief together with the previous total reached two thousand two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He became palace attendant and opening-the-feudatory, was raised to Duke of Changle, and his combined fief reached two thousand two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 四年，魏文帝東巡洛陽，與齊神武戰於河橋，惠力戰破之，大收降卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Emperor Wen of Wei toured east to Luoyang and fought Gao Huan at Heqiao; Hui fought hard and defeated him and greatly gathered surrendered troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Emperor Wen toured Luoyang and fought Gao Huan at Heqiao; Gan Hui fought fiercely, routed him, and took large numbers of prisoners.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷中領軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to commander of the central guard corps.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made commander of the central guard corps.

sentences.zh: 及高仲密舉北豫州來附，太祖帥師迎之。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi offered North Yuzhou in submission, the Grand Progenitor led troops to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi surrendered North Yuzhou, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched out to receive him.

sentences.zh: 軍至洛陽，齊神武於邙山將以邀我，太祖乃徙輜重於瀍曲，夜勒兵襲之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Luoyang, Gao Huan at Mount Mang was about to intercept them; the Grand Progenitor moved baggage to Chan Bend and at night ordered troops to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Near Luoyang, Gao Huan waited on Mount Mang to cut them off; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai shifted the baggage train to Chan Bend and struck by night.

sentences.zh: 及戰，惠為右軍，與中軍大破之，逐北數里，虜其步卒。

translations.literal: When they fought, Hui was the right army; with the center army he greatly defeated them, pursued north several li, and captured their foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the battle Gan Hui commanded the right wing; with the center he broke the enemy, chased them north for several li, and took their infantry.

sentences.zh: 齊神武兵乃萃於左軍，軍將趙貴等與戰不利，諸軍因之並退。

translations.literal: Gao Huan's troops then massed against the left army; army generals Zhao Gui and others fought unfavorably and all armies thereby retreated together.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan then concentrated against the left wing; Zhao Gui and the other commanders there were beaten, and the whole army fell back.

sentences.zh: 時會日暮，齊神武兵屢來攻惠，惠擊之，皆披靡。

translations.literal: As it happened at dusk, Gao Huan's troops repeatedly came to attack Hui; Hui struck them and all were routed.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Gao Huan's men attacked Gan Hui again and again; each time Gan Hui drove them off in rout.

sentences.zh: 至夜中，齊神武騎復來追惠，惠徐乃下馬，顧命廚人營食。

translations.literal: By midnight Gao Huan's cavalry again came pursuing Hui; Hui leisurely dismounted and turned to order the cook to prepare food.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Gao Huan's horsemen caught up with Gan Hui again; Gan Hui calmly dismounted and told the cook to serve a meal.

sentences.zh: 食訖，謂左右曰：「長安死，此中死，異乎？

translations.literal: When the meal was finished he said to those beside him: "To die in Chang'an, to die here—how are they different?"
translations.idiomatic: When he had eaten he said to his men: "Death in Chang'an, death here—what difference is there?"

sentences.zh: 」乃建旗鳴角，收諸敗軍而還。

translations.literal: He then raised banners and sounded horns, gathered the various defeated troops, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Then he raised his banners, sounded the horns, rallied the scattered units, and marched back.

sentences.zh: 齊神武追騎憚惠，疑有伏兵，不敢逼。

translations.literal: Gao Huan's pursuing cavalry feared Hui, suspected an ambush, and did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan's pursuers feared Gan Hui, suspected a trap, and would not come near.

sentences.zh: 至弘農，見太祖，陳賊形勢，恨其垂成之功，覆於一簣，於是歔欷不能自勝。

translations.literal: Reaching Hongnong, he saw the Grand Progenitor, reported the enemy situation, regretted that near-complete achievement was overturned by one basketful of earth, and thereupon sighed and sobbed unable to control himself.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongnong he saw Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, described the enemy's dispositions, and wept that victory had slipped away at the last moment.

sentences.zh: 太祖壯之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor approved his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai admired his bearing.

sentences.zh: 鳳字達摩，少沉深，有識度。

translations.literal: Feng, styled Damo, from youth was deep and reserved, with knowledge and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Feng, styled Damo, was grave and steady from youth, with judgment beyond his years.

sentences.zh: 大統末，襲父爵長樂郡公，尚太祖女。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong he inherited his father's title Duke of Changle commandery and married the Grand Progenitor's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Datong he inherited the dukedom of Changle and married a daughter of Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In Wei Deposed Emperor year two he was granted grand general of fast cavalry and opening-office three-division court equipage.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Deposed Emperor he received grand general of fast cavalry and opening-office three-division court equipage.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝三年，除左宮伯。

translations.literal: In Wei Respectful Emperor year three he was made left palace baron.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Respectful Emperor he was made left palace baron.

sentences.zh: 尋出為洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as governor of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as governor of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 徵拜大馭中大夫。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed grand master for managing chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and made grand master for managing chariots.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，追錄佐命之功，封鳳徐國公，增邑幷前五千戶。

translations.literal: In Baoding year four his merit in aiding the mandate was retrospectively recorded; Feng was enfeoffed Duke of Xu State with a fief together with the previous total of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding 4 (564) the court looked back on his father's founding service and enfeoffed Feng as Duke of Xu with a combined fief of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，拜柱國。

translations.literal: In Jianade year two he was appointed pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianade 2 (573) he was made pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 怡峯字景阜，遼西人也。

translations.literal: Yi Feng, styled Jingfu, was a native of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Feng, styled Jingfu, came from Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 本姓默臺，因避難改焉。

translations.literal: His original surname was Motai; because of fleeing hardship he changed it.
translations.idiomatic: His family had borne the surname Motai and changed it while taking refuge from turmoil.

sentences.zh: 高祖寬，燕遼西郡守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Kuan was administrator of Yan Liaoxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Kuan had been administrator of Yan Liaoxi commandery.

sentences.zh: 魏道武時，率戶歸朝，拜羽真，賜爵長虵公。

translations.literal: In Emperor Daowu of Wei's time he led households to submit to the court, was appointed yu-chen guard, and was granted the title Duke of Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Daowu of Wei he led his people in submission, entered imperial service as a yu-chen guard, and received the title Duke of Changshe.

sentences.zh: 曾祖文，冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wen was governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wen served as governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 峰少從征役，以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: Feng from youth followed campaigns and was renowned for fierce bravery.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Feng went on campaign from youth and won a name for bold fighting.

sentences.zh: 永安中，假龍驤將軍，為都將，從賀拔岳討万俟醜奴，以功授給事中、明威將軍，轉征虜將軍、都督，賜爵蒲陰縣男。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era he was acting general of soaring dragon and capital-guard commander; following Heba Yue against Wanqij Chounu, by merit he was granted gentleman attendant within the gates and general of clear might, transferred to general who campaigns against barbarians and area commander, and granted Viscount of Puyin county.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongan he served as acting general of soaring dragon and capital-guard commander; under Heba Yue against Wanqij Chounu he earned gentleman attendant within the gates, general of clear might, general who campaigns against barbarians, area commander, and the viscounty of Puyin.

sentences.zh: 及岳被害，峯與趙貴等同謀翊戴太祖。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed, Feng with Zhao Gui and others jointly plotted to support and install the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue was killed, Yi Feng joined Zhao Gui and the others in raising up Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 進爵為伯。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to earl.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to earl.

sentences.zh: 時原州刺史史歸猶為侯莫陳悅守，太祖令峰與侯莫陳崇討擒之。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Prefecture governor Shi Gui still garrisoned the province for Houmochen Yue; the Grand Progenitor ordered Feng with Houmochen Chong to campaign against and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Prefecture governor Shi Gui was still holding out for Houmochen Yue; Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent Yi Feng with Houmochen Chong to take him.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武與魏孝武帝構隙，帝頻勑太祖簡銳卒入衛京邑。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan and Emperor Xiaowu of Wei developed a rift, the emperor repeatedly ordered the Grand Progenitor to select sharp troops to enter and guard the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan and Emperor Xiaowu fell out, the emperor repeatedly ordered Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai to send picked troops to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃令峯與都督趙貴等率輕騎赴洛陽。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor then ordered Feng with area commander Zhao Gui and others to lead light cavalry to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then sent Yi Feng with Zhao Gui and others at the head of light cavalry to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 至潼關，值魏孝武西遷，峯即從太祖拔回洛，復潼關。

translations.literal: Reaching Tong Pass, it happened that Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west; Feng immediately followed the Grand Progenitor in seizing back Luoyang and recovering Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass they met Emperor Xiaowu fleeing west; Yi Feng at once followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in retaking Luoyang and securing Tong Pass again.

sentences.zh: 拜安東將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed general who pacifies the east and governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who pacifies the east and governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 尋轉大都督。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to grand commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand commander.

sentences.zh: 討曹泥有功，進爵華陽縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Cao Ni with merit, he was advanced in rank to Duke of Huayang county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service against Cao Ni he was raised to Duke of Huayang with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 大統［三］年，從太祖破竇泰於小關。

translations.literal: Datong (3) [emended: three] year, following the Grand Progenitor he broke Dou Tai at Xiao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 3 (537) he followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in defeating Dou Tai at Xiao Pass.

sentences.zh: 還，拜散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Returning, he was appointed regular attendant of scattered cavalry, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and three-division court equipage.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became regular attendant of scattered cavalry, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and three-division court equipage.

sentences.zh: 又從復弘農，破沙苑，進爵樂陵郡公。

translations.literal: Again following in recovering Hongnong and breaking Shaya, his rank was advanced to Duke of Leiling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He followed again in recovering Hongnong and breaking Shaya and was raised to Duke of Leiling.

sentences.zh: 仍與元季海、獨孤信復洛陽。

translations.literal: Still with Yuan Jihai and Dugu Xin he recovered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Yuan Jihai and Dugu Xin in recovering Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 峯率奇兵至成皋，入其郛，收其戶口而還。

translations.literal: Feng led surprise troops to Chenggao, entered its outer city, gathered its population, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Feng took a flying column to Chenggao, entered the suburbs, rounded up the people, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 東魏遣行臺任祥率步騎萬餘攻潁川，峯復以輕騎五百邀擊之，自是威名轉盛。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent mobile headquarters Ren Xiang leading over ten thousand foot and horse to attack Yingchuan; Feng again with five hundred light cavalry intercepted and struck them, and from this his fierce name grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Ren Xiang at the head of more than ten thousand men against Yingchuan; Yi Feng hit him with five hundred light horse, and his reputation as a fierce commander spread.

sentences.zh: 加授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was additionally granted opening-office three-division court equipage.
translations.idiomatic: He was further given opening-office three-division court equipage.

sentences.zh: 東魏圍洛陽，峯與季海守金墉。

translations.literal: When Eastern Wei besieged Luoyang, Feng with Jihai held Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei besieged Luoyang, Yi Feng and Yuan Jihai held Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 太祖至，圍解，即與東魏戰於河橋。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor arrived the siege was lifted, and they immediately fought Eastern Wei at Heqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's arrival lifted the siege, and they fought Eastern Wei at once at Heqiao.

sentences.zh: 時峯為左軍，不利，與李遠先還，太祖因此班師。

translations.literal: At the time Feng was the left army; the battle went badly, and with Li Yuan he returned first; the Grand Progenitor therefore withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Feng commanded the left wing; the fight went badly, and he withdrew ahead with Li Yuan, whereupon Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai pulled the army back.

sentences.zh: 詔原其罪。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned his offense.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forgave the fault.

sentences.zh: 拜東西北三夏州諸軍事、夏州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander of all military affairs of the three Xia provinces of east, northwest, and west, and governor of Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of the three Xia provinces—east, northwest, and west—and governor of Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 後與于謹討劉平伏，從解玉壁圍，平栢穀塢，竝有功。

translations.literal: Later, with Yu Jin he campaigned against Liu Pingfu; following in relieving the siege of Yubi and pacifying Baigu Stockade, in each case he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Yu Jin against Liu Pingfu and shared in relieving Yubi and taking Baigu Stockade.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史宇文仲和反，峯與于謹討之。

translations.literal: When Liang Province governor Yuwen Zhonghe rebelled, Feng with Yu Jin campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang governor Yuwen Zhonghe rebelled, Yi Feng marched against him with Yu Jin.

sentences.zh: 十五年，東魏圍潁川，峰與趙貴赴援。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Eastern Wei besieged Yingchuan; Feng with Zhao Gui went to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Eastern Wei besieged Yingchuan; Yi Feng and Zhao Gui marched to its relief.

sentences.zh: 至南陽，遇疾卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: Reaching Nanyang, he encountered illness and died; at the time he was fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died at Nanyang, aged fifty.

sentences.zh: 峰沉毅有膽略，得士卒心，當時號為驍將。

translations.literal: Feng was deep, resolute, and possessed daring strategy; he won the hearts of officers and soldiers, and at the time was styled a fierce general.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Feng was steady, bold, and shrewd in battle; his men trusted him, and contemporaries called him a fierce commander.

sentences.zh: 太祖嗟悼者久之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor sighed and mourned for him a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai mourned him at length.

sentences.zh: 贈華州刺史，諡曰襄威。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given governor of Huazhou; his posthumous title was Xiangwei.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made governor of Huazhou with the posthumous name Xiangwei, "Assisting in Might."

sentences.zh: 子昂嗣。

translations.literal: His son Ang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 官至開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He reached the office of opening-office three-division court equipage.
translations.idiomatic: Ang rose to opening-office three-division court equipage.

sentences.zh: 朝廷追錄峰功，封昂鄭國公。

translations.literal: The court retrospectively recorded Feng's achievements and enfeoffed Ang Duke of Zheng State.
translations.idiomatic: The court looked back on Yi Feng's service and enfeoffed Ang as Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 昂弟光，少以峯勳，賜爵安平縣侯，起家員外散騎常侍，累遷司土中大夫、左武伯，出為汾、涇、豳三州刺史，加開府儀同三司，進爵龍河縣公。

translations.literal: Ang's younger brother Guang, in youth on account of Feng's merit, was granted the marquisate of Anping county, began his career as regular attendant of scattered cavalry outside service, was progressively transferred to central grand prefect supervising earth and left martial earl, went out as governor of Fen, Jing, and Bin provinces, was given opening-office three-division court equipage, and advanced in rank to Duke of Longhe county.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's younger brother Guang entered service young on Yi Feng's merit, was made Marquis of Anping, rose from regular attendant of scattered cavalry to central grand prefect supervising earth and left martial earl, served as governor of Fen, Jing, and Bin provinces, received opening-office three-division court equipage, and was raised to Duke of Longhe.

sentences.zh: 光弟春，少知名，歷官吏部下大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Guang's younger brother Chun was known from youth, served as grand prefect of officials in the ministry office and equal-to-three-division protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's younger brother Chun was known from youth and served as grand prefect of officials in the ministry office with equal-to-three-division protocol.

sentences.zh: 劉亮中山人也，本名道德。

translations.literal: Liu Liang was a man of Zhongshan; his original name was Daode.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang came from Zhongshan; his original name was Daode.

sentences.zh: 祖佑連，魏蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Youlian was governor of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Youlian was governor of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父持真，鎮遠將軍、領民酋長。

translations.literal: His father Chizhen was distant-quelling general and tribal chieftain commanding the people.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chizhen was distant-quelling general and tribal chieftain commanding the people.

sentences.zh: 魏大統中，以亮著勳，追贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司、恒州刺史。

translations.literal: In Western Wei's Datong era, because Liang had distinguished merit, he was posthumously awarded general of chariots and cavalry, equal-to-three-division protocol, and governor of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Western Wei's Datong era Liu Liang's service was rewarded posthumously with general of chariots and cavalry, equal-to-three-division protocol, and governor of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 亮少倜儻，有從橫計略，姿貌魁傑，見者憚之。

translations.literal: Liang in youth was bold and free; he had horizontal stratagems, bearing and appearance tall and outstanding—those who saw him feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang was bold and resourceful from youth, with a imposing bearing that intimidated those who met him.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，以都督從賀拔岳西征，解岐州圍，擊侯伏侯元進、万俟道洛、万俟醜奴、宿勤明達及諸賊，亮常先鋒陷陣。

translations.literal: At the start of Putai, as commander he followed Heba Yue on the western campaign, relieved the siege of Qi Prefecture, attacked Hou Fuhou Yuanjin, Wanqij Daoluo, Wanqij Chounu, Suqin Mingda, and various bandits; Liang was often vanguard breaking formations.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Putai he followed Heba Yue west as commander, lifted the siege of Qi, and fought Hou Fuhou Yuanjin, Wanqij Daoluo, Wanqij Chounu, Suqin Mingda, and other rebels, often leading the charge himself.

sentences.zh: 以功拜大都督，封廣興縣子，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed grand commander, enfeoffed Viscount of Guangxing county, fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made grand commander and enfeoffed Viscount of Guangxing with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳悅害岳，亮與諸將謀迎太祖。

translations.literal: Houmochen Yue killed Yue; Liang with the various generals plotted to welcome the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue murdered Heba Yue, Liu Liang and the other commanders plotted to raise up Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 悅平，悅之黨豳州刺史孫定兒仍據州不下，涇、秦、靈等諸州悉與定兒相應，衆至數萬，推定兒為主，以拒義師。

translations.literal: When Yue was pacified, Yue's partisan Bin Province governor Sun Ding'er still held the province and would not submit; Jing, Qin, Ling, and other provinces all responded to Ding'er; the host reached tens of thousands, made Ding'er lord, to resist the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: After Houmochen Yue was crushed, his ally Sun Ding'er still held Bin Province; Jing, Qin, Ling, and other prefectures rallied to him until his force numbered tens of thousands, with Ding'er as their leader opposing the loyalists.

sentences.zh: 太祖令亮襲之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered Liang to raid him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered Liu Liang to attack him.

sentences.zh: 定兒以義兵猶遠，未為之備。

translations.literal: Ding'er thought the righteous army was still distant and did not prepare against them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ding'er assumed the loyalists were still far off and made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 亮乃將二十騎，先豎纛於近城高嶺，即馳入城中。

translations.literal: Liang then led twenty horsemen, first erected a banner standard on a high ridge near the city, then galloped into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang took twenty horsemen, first raised a banner on a ridge near the city, then galloped straight in.

sentences.zh: 定兒方置酒高會，卒見亮至，衆皆駭愕，莫知所為。

translations.literal: Ding'er was just holding a grand wine banquet; suddenly seeing Liang arrive, the crowd were all startled and dismayed, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ding'er was at a banquet when Liu Liang appeared; the whole company was stunned and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 亮乃麾兵斬定兒，縣首，號令賊黨。

translations.literal: Liang then waved troops to behead Ding'er, displayed the head, and proclaimed orders to the bandit partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang had his men behead Sun Ding'er, displayed the head, and issued orders to the rebel ranks.

sentences.zh: 仍遙指城外纛，命二騎曰：「出追大軍。

translations.literal: Still pointing distantly at the banner outside the city, he ordered two horsemen, saying: "Go out and pursue the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Still pointing at the banner on the ridge outside the city, he told two riders: "Go out and pursue the main army.

sentences.zh: 」賊黨忷懼，一時降服。

translations.literal: " The bandit partisans were alarmed and fearful, and at once submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels panicked and surrendered on the spot.

sentences.zh: 於是諸州群賊，皆即歸款。

translations.literal: Thereupon the bandits of the various provinces all immediately came to pledge allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the rebels of the surrounding provinces submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 亮以勇敢見知，為時名將，兼屢陳謀策，多合機宜。

translations.literal: Liang was known for his bravery, was a famous general of the age, and moreover repeatedly offered stratagems, mostly fitting the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang was famed for courage and repeatedly offered plans that fit the moment; he was counted among the great commanders of the day.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃謂之曰：「卿文武兼資，即孤之孔明也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thus said to him: "You combine civil and military talents—you are my Kongming.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai told him: "You unite civil and military talent—you are my Kongming.

sentences.zh: 」乃賜名亮，並賜姓侯莫陳氏。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was granted the name Liang, and also granted the surname Houmochen.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon received the name Liang and the surname Houmochen.

sentences.zh: 十年，出為東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he went out as governor of East Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was sent out as governor of East Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 為政清淨，百姓安之。

translations.literal: His governance was pure and tranquil; the common people were secure under him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was clean and quiet, and the people lived securely under him.

sentences.zh: 在職三歲，卒於州，時年四十。

translations.literal: In office three years, he died in the province; at the time his age was forty.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he died in the province, aged forty.

sentences.zh: 喪還京師，太祖親臨之，泣而謂人曰：「股肱喪矣，腹心何寄！

translations.literal: The coffin returned to the capital; the Grand Progenitor personally came to the funeral, weeping and saying to people: "My arms and thighs are lost—where shall the heart be entrusted!
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin reached the capital Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai came in person, wept, and said: "I have lost my arms and thighs—where can I place my heart now!

sentences.zh: 」令鴻臚卿監護喪事。

translations.literal: " He ordered the grand master of ceremonies to supervise the funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the grand master of ceremonies to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 追贈太尉，諡曰襄，配享太祖廟庭。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded grand commandant, posthumous title Xiang, paired sacrifice at the Grand Progenitor's temple courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand commandant with the posthumous name Xiang and given a place in Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 子昶，尚太祖女西河長公主。

translations.literal: His son Chang married the Grand Progenitor's daughter, the Princess of West River.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang married Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's daughter, the Princess of West River.

sentences.zh: 大象中，位至柱國、秦靈二州總管。

translations.literal: In Daxiang, he reached the posts of pillar-of-state and area commander of Qin and Ling provinces.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daxiang era he rose to pillar-of-state and area commander of Qin and Ling provinces.

sentences.zh: 以亮功，封彭國公，邑五千戶。

translations.literal: On account of Liang's merit, he was enfeoffed Duke of Peng state, fief five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For Liu Liang's service he was enfeoffed Duke of Peng with five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 昶弟靖，天水郡守。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Jing was prefect of Tianshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Jing was prefect of Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 靖弟恭，開府儀同三司、饒陽縣伯。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Gong was opening-office three-division court equipage and Baron of Raoyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's younger brother Gong held opening-office three-division court equipage and the barony of Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 恭弟幹，上儀同三司、褒中侯。

translations.literal: Gong's younger brother Gan was upper equal-to-three-division protocol and Marquis of Baozhong.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's younger brother Gan held upper equal-to-three-division protocol and the marquisate of Baozhong.

sentences.zh: 王德字天恩，代郡武川人也。

translations.literal: Wang De styled Tian'en was a man of Wuchuan in Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De, styled Tian'en, came from Wuchuan in Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 少善騎射，雖不經師訓，而以孝悌見稱。

translations.literal: In youth skilled at mounted archery; though he did not receive teacher's instruction, he was acclaimed for filial piety and fraternity.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at riding and archery from youth; though he had no formal schooling, he was praised for filial piety and brotherly respect.

sentences.zh: 魏永安二年，從爾朱榮討元顥，攻河內，應募先登。

translations.literal: In Wei's second year of Yongan, he followed Erzhu Rong to campaign against Yuan Hao, attacked Henei, answered the levy and was first to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongan 2 (529) he followed Erzhu Rong against Yuan Hao, attacked Henei, and was first over the wall when volunteers were called.

sentences.zh: 以功除討夷將軍，進爵內官縣子。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed general for punishing the barbarians and advanced in rank to Viscount of Neiguan county.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made general for punishing the barbarians and raised to Viscount of Neiguan.

sentences.zh: 又從賀拔岳討万俟醜奴，平之。

translations.literal: Again he followed Heba Yue to campaign against Wanqij Chounu and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Heba Yue against Wanqij Chounu and helped pacify him.

sentences.zh: 別封深澤縣男，邑二百戶，加龍驤將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: Separately enfeoffed Baron of Shenze county, fief two hundred households; added general of soaring dragon and palace attendant-in-regular service.
translations.idiomatic: He was separately enfeoffed Baron of Shenze with two hundred households and given general of soaring dragon and palace attendant-in-regular service.

sentences.zh: 及侯莫陳悅害岳，德與寇洛等定議翊戴太祖。

translations.literal: When Houmochen Yue killed Yue, De with Kou Luo and others fixed the plan to support and install the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue murdered Heba Yue, Wang De and Kou Luo and others resolved to raise up Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 加征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫、平涼郡守。

translations.literal: Added campaign-west general, golden-purple light-in-the-distance grandee, and prefect of Pingliang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made campaign-west general, golden-purple light-in-the-distance grandee, and prefect of Pingliang commandery.

sentences.zh: 德雖不知書，至於斷決處分，良吏無以過也。

translations.literal: Though De did not know books, as for decisions and dispositions, fine officials could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De could not read, yet in judgment and administration no capable official could match him.

sentences.zh: 涇州所部五郡，而德常為最。

translations.literal: Of the five commanderies under Jing Province, De was always ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Among the five commanderies under Jing Province, Wang De's district was always ranked first.

sentences.zh: 德性厚重廉慎，言行無擇。

translations.literal: De's nature was weighty, thick, honest and cautious; in speech and conduct there was no choosing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De was grave, honest, and cautious, consistent in word and deed.

sentences.zh: 母年幾百歲，後德終。

translations.literal: His mother lived to nearly a hundred; she survived De.
translations.idiomatic: His mother lived to nearly a hundred and outlived him.

sentences.zh: 子慶，小名公奴，性謹厚。

translations.literal: His son Qing, pet name Gongnu, nature careful and thick.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qing—pet name Gongnu—was cautious and steady by nature.

sentences.zh: 官至開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: His office reached opening-office three-division court equipage.
translations.idiomatic: Qing rose to opening-office three-division court equipage.

sentences.zh: 初德喪父，家貧無以葬，乃賣公奴幷一女以營葬事。

translations.literal: At first when De mourned his father, the family was poor with no means to bury him; he therefore sold Gongnu together with one daughter to arrange the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang De mourned his father the family was too poor to bury him, so he sold Gongnu and a daughter to pay for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 因遭兵亂，不復相知。

translations.literal: Because they encountered military disorder, they no longer knew each other's whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: War then scattered them and they lost contact.

sentences.zh: 及德在平涼始得之，遂名曰慶。

translations.literal: When De was at Pingliang he at last found him, and thereupon named him Qing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang De was at Pingliang he found the boy at last and named him Qing, "Celebration."

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：梁禦等負將率之材，蘊驍銳之氣，遭逢喪亂，馳騖干戈，艱難險阻備嘗，而功名未立。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Liang Yu and others bore the talent of commanders, harbored fierce and sharp spirit; encountering disorder and ruin, they galloped amidst arms, tasted every hardship, peril and obstacle, yet fame and achievement were not established.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Liang Yu and the others had the makings of commanders and the mettle of fierce warriors; they endured the chaos of war and every hardship, yet won no lasting fame.

sentences.zh: 及殷憂啟聖，豫奉興王，參謀締構之初，宣力經綸之始，遂得連衡灌、酈，方駕張、徐，可謂遇其時也。

translations.literal: When deep sorrow opened the sage, they beforehand served the founding king, counseled at the beginning of founding construction, displayed strength at the beginning of ordering the realm—thereby they were able to link with Guan and Li, drive abreast with Zhang and Xu; one may say they met their time.
translations.idiomatic: When sorrow gave way to a founding sage they served the rising dynasty from the first, counselled at the start of its construction, and labored at the beginning of its ordering—so they could rank with Guan and Li and stand beside Zhang and Xu; they had truly met their moment.

sentences.zh: 竝中年即世，遠志未申，惜哉！

translations.literal: Both at middle age passed from the world; distant aspirations were not fulfilled—pity!
translations.idiomatic: All died in middle age with their greater ambitions unfulfilled—alas!

sentences.zh: 惠、德本以果毅知名，而能率由孝道，難矣。

translations.literal: Hui and De originally were known for resolute courage, yet able to follow filial piety—difficult indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ganhui and Wang De were famed for bold resolve, yet also lived by filial duty—no small thing.

sentences.zh: 圖史所歎，何以加焉。

translations.literal: What history's records sigh at—how could one add to it?
translations.idiomatic: Histories can scarcely praise them enough.

sentences.zh: 勇者不必有仁，斯不然矣。

translations.literal: The brave need not have benevolence—this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: The saying that courage need not bring benevolence does not apply here.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
